LESSON: GUIDED READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.7: Guided Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does repetition aid in reading fluency?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. apply effective reading strategies in extracting information from different sources
2. recognise the importance of repetition in improving reading fluency
3. identify key words and phrases in reading texts
4. apply pauses effectively to emphasise key points in texts
5. appreciate the role of appropriate fluency for effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED READING
Subject: MANDARIN · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Reading helps you succeed in MANDARIN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Apply effective reading strategies in extracting information from different sources

What this means
In this part you learn to apply effective reading strategies in extracting information from different sources. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply effective reading strategies in extracting information from different sources.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply effective reading strategies in extracting information from different sources. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Recognise the importance of repetition in improving reading fluency

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise the importance of repetition in improving reading fluency. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise the importance of repetition in improving reading fluency.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise the importance of repetition in improving reading fluency. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Identify key words and phrases in reading texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify key words and phrases in reading texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify key words and phrases in reading texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify key words and phrases in reading texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply pauses effectively to emphasise key points in texts

What this means
In this part you learn to apply pauses effectively to emphasise key points in texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply pauses effectively to emphasise key points in texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply pauses effectively to emphasise key points in texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 5: Appreciate the role of appropriate fluency for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of appropriate fluency for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of appropriate fluency for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of appropriate fluency for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: apply effective reading strategies in extracting information from different sources)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Reading to a partner. (skill: recognise the importance of repetition in improving reading fluency)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: identify key words and phrases in reading texts)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: apply pauses effectively to emphasise key points in texts)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: apply effective reading strategies in extracting information from different sources.
3. Practise this skill: recognise the importance of repetition in improving reading fluency.
4. Practise this skill: identify key words and phrases in reading texts.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Guided Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does repetition aid in reading fluency?
2. How can pronunciation affect communication?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: apply effective reading strategies in extracting information from different sources.
5. Be able to: recognise the importance of repetition in improving reading fluency.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
